title: The Dashboard loads fast, and one slow tile does not block the rest
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the dashboard (signed in with the Reports permission) with a workplace that has a realistic amount of data.
custom_steps:
1. This case checks the dashboard’s speed and stability targets — how quickly the tiles load, and that one slow tile cannot take down the whole dashboard. Those targets are measured with developer performance tooling, so this is NOT a check a manual tester runs by hand.
  2. The user-visible part of this — that one tile can fail or be slow while the other five keep working — is checked by hand in the per-tile loading / failure case in Section 6; run it there.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The dashboard meets its speed targets (tiles load quickly, and the first full load is fast), measured with developer performance tooling — not by eye.
  • If one tile’s data is slow or fails, only that tile shows a failure; the other five still load. (The user-visible half of this is run by hand in the Section 6 loading / failure case.)

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Dashboard v1 — Technical Implementation Plan (sources/Dashboard-v1-Technical-Implementation-Plan.md, 2026-09-16). It informs, it does not overrule the PRD (Rules 30/57).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • Tech plan NFR-001: “No dashboard query may exceed 500 ms; anything above is treated as a defect and alerted. Per-tile server time targets p95 ≤ 250 ms; the six-tile first load targets p95 ≤ 1 s (a slight overrun is acceptable). Every dashboard statement carries a 2 s MAX_EXECUTION_TIME circuit breaker, and a query that trips it fails only its own tile (FR-021)”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

AUTOMATION: HOLD - not manually testable (performance budget and per-tile circuit breaker are developer/automated checks)
